objection.quote: Need a rigorous proof that (1) only finitely many primes can ever be forced as new restrictions, or more carefully: the set A of all positive integers m that share a factor with every a_i
objection.witness: The missing statement is a proved all-terms large-prime-erasure lemma: membership must depend only on primes in one finite set, with every term involving a larger prime dominated by a smaller term having the same relevant small-prime support. The quote explicitly says that this still needs a rigorous proof.
objection.load_bearing: Without finiteness, no finite product L can capture all membership conditions, so translation invariance cannot be established.
